aliases: NA62 refined measurement of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar branching ratio (2026 update)

announced.note: Date of the CERN news item about results 'just presented at the 2026 La Thuile conference'; the talk itself may be earlier.

claim.quote: With results from data collected between 2016 and 2022, the analysis gives ${\rm B}_{\rm 2016-2024}(K^+\to\pi^+\nu\bar{\nu}) = \left(9.6^{+1.9}_{-1.8}\right)\times10^{-11}$, corresponding to a relative precision of $20\%$.

date.note: This is a CERN news article about a conference presentation (2026 La Thuile conference) reporting results 'just presented at the 2026 La Thuile conference' (the page does not call the value preliminary); the full measurement was subsequently posted as arXiv:2607.16413 (submitted 17 July 2026, CERN-EP-2026-214), which restates the identical central value and is now the source for the result's claim (A16 forbids sourcing claim.quote to a press release).

key_value.note: Branching ratio in units of 10⁻¹¹; the central value is shown as a bare number without a unit. Confirmed verbatim in the arXiv:2607.16413 abstract and corroborated by the earlier CERN news article.

key_value_text.value: B(K⁺ → π⁺ ν ν̄) = (9.6+1.9−1.8) × 10⁻¹¹, combining data collected 2016-2024 (including newly analysed 2023-2024 data: B_2023-2024 = (7.2+2.3−2.1) × 10⁻¹¹), a relative precision of 20%

name: NA62 refined measurement of the K⁺ → π⁺νν̄ branching ratio (2026 update)
notes: Sourced to arXiv:2607.16413 (CERN-EP-2026-214, submitted 17 July 2026), 'Measurement of the branching ratio of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay', which restates the (9.6+1.9−1.8) × 10⁻¹¹ central value first announced at the 2026 La Thuile conference. The earlier CERN news article about the conference talk is cited only as corroboration.

An intermediate conference-proceedings preprint, arXiv:2604.12649 ('New measurement of K+ -> pi+ nu nubar branching ratio at the NA62 experiment', submitted 14 April 2026), also restates this value from a preliminary analysis; the later, full measurement paper arXiv:2607.16413 is used instead as the primary claim source.
As of 2026-09-17 arXiv:2607.16413 has no journal DOI yet (CERN preprint report number CERN-EP-2026-214); publication.doi is left null rather than guessed.

significance.locator: home.cern news article, 4 March 2026 (no sigma value restated for this update)
significance.note: Neither the arXiv:2607.16413 abstract nor the CERN news article states a sigma value for this specific combined 2016-2024 measurement (the abstract instead states a 20% relative precision); left null rather than assumed unchanged from the 2025 discovery-level result.

summary.plain: An update presented at the 2026 La Thuile conference: NA62 added data from 2023 and 2024 to its earlier data and measured the rare kaon decay K⁺→π⁺νν̄ to a relative precision of 20%. CERN's news item says the uncertainty is 40% smaller than before; the paper says the value is consistent with Standard Model predictions.
summary.technical: Branching ratio B(K⁺→π⁺νν̄) from the 2023-2024 data: (7.2 +2.3 −2.1)×10⁻¹¹; with the results from data collected between 2016 and 2022 the analysis gives B_2016-2024 = (9.6 +1.9 −1.8)×10⁻¹¹, a relative precision of 20%, which the paper says is consistent with Standard Model predictions. CERN's news item on the La Thuile presentation gives the uncertainty as 40% smaller than before.

title: Measurement of the branching ratio of the K+ -> pi+ nu nubar decay
why_it_matters: CERN's news item says the branching ratio of this decay can be predicted theoretically with a very high degree of precision, so the decay is extremely sensitive to new physics beyond the Standard Model; the paper says the updated value is consistent with Standard Model predictions.
